## Purpose and entry points
OpenToonz is a native 2D-animation application, built primarily in C/C++. The desktop executable starts at `toonz/sources/toonz/main.cpp`; its application shell and main window are in `toonz/sources/toonz/tapp.cpp` and `toonz/sources/toonz/mainwindow.cpp`. The source build graph begins at `toonz/sources/CMakeLists.txt`.

## Scene and timeline domain model
The central editable model is a scene containing levels, columns, cells, palettes, cameras, stage objects, and an exposure sheet (Xsheet). `toonz/sources/toonzlib/toonzscene.cpp`, `toonz/sources/toonzlib/txsheet.cpp`, and `toonz/sources/toonzlib/txshlevel.cpp` define this persistent animation domain. UI commands, drawing tools, and import/export operate against this model rather than directly on rendered pixels.

## Desktop UI and interaction layer
Qt-facing reusable controls, schematic editors, palette viewers, and docking infrastructure reside in `toonz/sources/toonzqt/`; application-specific panels/viewers reside in `toonz/sources/toonz/`. The UI drives command-oriented editing and displays the Xsheet, scene viewer, filmstrip, function editor, and FX schematic. Relevant paths: `toonz/sources/toonz/xsheetviewer.cpp`, `toonz/sources/toonz/sceneviewer.cpp`, `toonz/sources/toonzqt/fxschematicscene.cpp`.

## Drawing, vector/raster, and cleanup pipeline
Tools translate user input into changes to vector, raster, or Toonz raster levels and palettes. The tool implementation boundary is `toonz/sources/tnztools/tool.cpp`, with brush implementations such as `toonz/sources/tnztools/toonzrasterbrushtool.cpp` and `toonz/sources/tnztools/toonzvectorbrushtool.cpp`. Raster/vector primitives and operations are lower-level common libraries: `toonz/sources/common/traster/traster.cpp`, `toonz/sources/common/tvectorimage/tvectorimage.cpp`, and `toonz/sources/common/trop/trop.cpp`. Cleanup and vectorization are domain services in `toonz/sources/toonzlib/tcleanupper.cpp` and `toonz/sources/toonzlib/tcenterlinevectorizer.cpp`.

## FX graph and rendering
Columns and image sources feed an FX DAG, which resolves dependencies and renders frame/image tiles with caching. Core graph and renderer paths are `toonz/sources/toonzlib/fxdag.cpp`, `toonz/sources/common/tfx/tfx.cpp`, and `toonz/sources/common/tfx/trenderer.cpp`. Built-in effect implementations are compiled from `toonz/sources/stdfx/`, while FX metadata/layout registrations are deployed in `stuff/profiles/layouts/fxs/`. GPU-backed shader effects bridge XML definitions and GLSL programs under `stuff/library/shaders/`.

## Media I/O and output boundary
The image abstraction and generic I/O layer are in `toonz/sources/common/timage/timage.cpp` and `toonz/sources/common/timage_io/timage_io.cpp`. Format adapters are segregated under `toonz/sources/image/`, including FFmpeg-backed video codecs in `toonz/sources/image/ffmpeg/tiio_ffmpeg.cpp`, OpenEXR in `toonz/sources/image/exr/tiio_exr.cpp`, and native Toonz formats under `toonz/sources/image/tzp/`. Audio I/O is similarly separate in `toonz/sources/sound/`. Rendering/output UI commands ultimately use scene/output properties and movie rendering services: `toonz/sources/toonz/rendercommand.cpp`, `toonz/sources/toonzlib/outputproperties.cpp`, `toonz/sources/toonzlib/movierenderer.cpp`.

## Extensibility, resources, and external execution
Runtime plugins are loaded through `toonz/sources/common/tsystem/tpluginmanager.cpp`; sample effect plugins are separate CMake targets in `plugins/blur/blur.cpp` and `plugins/geom/geom.cpp`. Default profiles, menus, FX lists, palettes, brushes, and project-folder conventions are packaged under `stuff/`, notably `stuff/profiles/layouts/` and `stuff/studiopalette/`. Optional render-farm infrastructure is a TCP/IP client/controller/server subsystem under `toonz/sources/toonzfarm/tfarm/`, `toonz/sources/toonzfarm/tfarmcontroller/`, and `toonz/sources/toonzfarm/tfarmserver/`.

## Runtime and platform dependencies
The application uses Qt for desktop UI and OpenGL support (`toonz/sources/common/tgl/tgl.cpp`), with platform-specific code for Windows, macOS, Linux, and BSD. Bundled dependencies include image codecs/compression, OpenGL extension loading, linear algebra, and painting support: `thirdparty/libjpeg-turbo/`, `thirdparty/tiff-4.0.3/`, `thirdparty/glew/glew-1.9.0/`, and `thirdparty/libmypaint/`. CI explicitly targets Linux, macOS, and Windows through `.github/workflows/`.
